the artist

Yue Minjun

b. 1962, China

Yue Minjun is one of the leading figures of Cynical Realism, a post-Tiananmen art movement defined by ironic, self-aware commentary on contemporary Chinese life. His trademark is the endlessly grinning self-portrait, cloned across a scene in dozens of identical faces.

The laughter is exaggerated, almost grotesque, a mask that hides as much as it reveals. By inserting himself repeatedly into historical, political, or even absurd scenarios, Yue turns the crowd into a chorus of complicity, a visual metaphor for conformity, denial, and the performance of happiness under pressure.

In works like Execution (1995), which became the most expensive piece of Chinese contemporary art at auction at the time, this multiplied grin becomes both unsettling and magnetic, proof that the image you project can dominate the truth beneath.
